Find y′ for y=4x2sin⁡x.

a
xcos⁡x+2xsin⁡xsin⁡x
b
2x2sin⁡x−8xsin⁡xsin⁡x
c
2x2sin⁡xsin⁡x−xsin⁡x
d
8xsin⁡x+2x2cos⁡xsin⁡x
e
−2x2cos⁡xcos⁡x+8xsin⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product and chain rules, y′=8x√sin(x)+2x²cos(x)/√sin(x)=(8xsin(x)+2x²cos(x))/√sin(x), which matches option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
This question requires the product rule. Let $u(x)=4{x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Then

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=8x,\,{v}^{′}(x)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(8x)(\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x})+(4{x}^{2})(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}) \\  & =8x\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}+\frac{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =\frac{8x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find y′ for y=4x2sin⁡x.

a
xcos⁡x+2xsin⁡xsin⁡x
b
2x2sin⁡x−8xsin⁡xsin⁡x
c
2x2sin⁡xsin⁡x−xsin⁡x
d
8xsin⁡x+2x2cos⁡xsin⁡x
e
−2x2cos⁡xcos⁡x+8xsin⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

This question requires the product rule. Let u(x)=4x2 and v(x)=sin⁡x. Then

u′(x)=8x,v′(x)=cos⁡x2sin⁡x.

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate v.

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

y′=dydx=u′(x)⋅v(x)+u(x)⋅v′(x)=(8x)(sin⁡x)+(4x2)(cos⁡x2sin⁡x)=8xsin⁡x+2x2cos⁡xsin⁡x=8xsin⁡x+2x2cos⁡xsin⁡x.

content.worked_solution:
This question requires the product rule. Let $u(x)=4{x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Then

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=8x,\,{v}^{′}(x)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(8x)(\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x})+(4{x}^{2})(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}) \\  & =8x\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}+\frac{2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =\frac{8x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find y′ for y=ln⁡x2x.

a
ln⁡x−2ln⁡x
b
1−2ln⁡xln⁡x

1+2ln⁡x2x2ln⁡x
d
1−2ln⁡x4x2ln⁡x

decision.explanation: Write y=(1/2)x^{-1}√ln(x). The product and chain rules give y′=-√ln(x)/(2x²)+1/(4x²√ln(x))=(1-2ln(x))/(4x²√ln(x)), matching option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
We use the quotient rule with the numerator $u(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}$ and the denominator $v(x)=2x.$ 

Differentiating $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ we have

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{2x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}},\,{v}^{′}(x)=2.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $u.$

Now, applying the quotient rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{2x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}})(2x)-(\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x})(2)}{(2x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}-2\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4{x}^{2}\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

This question requires the product rule. Let $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)={sin}^{3}⁡x.$ Then

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=2x,\,{v}^{′}(x)=3{sin}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(2x)({sin}^{3}⁡x)+({x}^{2})(3{sin}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =2x{sin}^{3}⁡x+3{x}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x})|}_{x=0} & =2\cdot 0\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡(0)+3\cdot {0}^{2}\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
